title: OLS, 1M rows
label: OLS, 1M rows

environment.threads: One thread everywhere: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, OMP_NUM_THREADS, MKL_NUM_THREADS, VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS and BLIS_NUM_THREADS set to 1 for R (OpenBLAS), numpy and GPBoost (OpenMP). phit and phit-polyfill are single-threaded.

code.R:
fit <- lm(
  y ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9 + x10,
  data = d
)
table <- coef(summary(fit))
code.statsmodels:
fit = smf.ols(
    'y ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6 + x7 + x8 + x9 + x10',
    data=d,
).fit()
coefficients, standard_errors = fit.params, fit.bse

description: Least-squares fit of a linear model from a formula, returning coefficients and standard errors. Implementations: the phit extension, phit-polyfill, R lm(), and statsmodels OLS.
method: Each run is a fresh process. Each implementation runs once as a warm-up, then the 4 alternate for 7 rounds in a rotated order. The time runs from the data already in memory in the runtime's usual structure (PHP arrays of columns, an R data.frame, a pandas DataFrame, or numpy arrays for GPBoost) to holding the coefficients and standard errors, and includes building the model matrix from the formula. Reading the CSV file is outside the timing. Every process runs under bench/peakmem.c. Memory is the process's peak anonymous memory, data included: its own allocations, without the file pages it maps, from RssAnon in /proc, sampled every millisecond. The peak resident set size, which counts those pages, and each runtime's baseline memory with its libraries loaded and no data are recorded beside it. OLS has no iterations. phit and phit-polyfill solve by column-scaled SVD. R lm() uses a Householder QR (LINPACK dqrls). statsmodels OLS.fit() uses its default method, "pinv": the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse by SVD.
reproduce: # Linux: build bench/peakmem.c and put it on the PATH
